title: Quran Knowledge
description: A question bank on Quran structure, revelation, narratives, teachings and careful reading, with explanations and source references.
difficultyMethod: Editorial classification; not calibrated from learner response data. Advanced means greater reasoning depth within this subject, not a scholarly qualification.

review.referenceCheck: Primary-text references checked during preparation; this is not independent scholarly approval.

selectionHints.unknownResponse: Handle I am not sure as a UI action, not as a fifth answer option.

questions.question: How many surahs are in the Quran?
questions.explanation: The Quran's standard surah index contains 114 chapters, beginning with Al-Fatihah and ending with An-Nas.

questions.question: In the structure of the Quran, what is a surah?

options.text: A translation language
A chapter
A recitation recording
A type of commentary

questions.explanation: A surah is a chapter of the Quran. Each chapter contains ayahs, commonly called verses in English.

references.label: Quran Foundation: chapter and verse-key documentation

questions.question: In a Quran reference such as 12:4, what does the second number identify?

options.text: The printed page in every edition
The number of words in the chapter
The ayah or verse within the surah
The year of revelation

questions.explanation: Quran references use the surah number followed by the ayah number. Page numbers can differ between printed editions.

references.label: Quran Foundation: chapter and verse-key documentation

questions.question: Which surah comes first in the Quran's standard written order?

options.text: Al-Baqarah
Al-'Alaq
An-Nas
Al-Fatihah

questions.explanation: Al-Fatihah is the first surah in the standard written order. This question concerns written order, not the chronology of revelation.

questions.question: Which surah comes last in the Quran's standard written order?

options.text: An-Nas
Al-Falaq
Al-Ikhlas
Al-Kawthar

questions.explanation: An-Nas is surah 114, the final chapter in the standard written order.

questions.question: According to Quran 12:2, in which language was the Quran revealed?

options.text: Hebrew
Arabic
Aramaic
Persian

questions.explanation: Yusuf 12:2 identifies the revelation as an Arabic Quran and links this with understanding.

questions.question: Which month is associated with the revelation of the Quran in Quran 2:185?

options.text: Muharram
Rajab
Ramadan
Dhul-Hijjah

questions.explanation: Al-Baqarah 2:185 names Ramadan as the month in which the Quran was revealed.

questions.question: Which night is named in Quran 97:1 in connection with the Quran being sent down?

options.text: The night before Eid al-Adha
The first night of Muharram
The night of every full moon
Laylat al-Qadr

questions.explanation: Al-Qadr 97:1 identifies Laylat al-Qadr as the night of the Quran's descent. The verse does not specify a numbered night of Ramadan.

questions.question: Which passage is associated with the beginning of revelation in Sahih al-Bukhari 3?

options.text: The opening verses of Al-'Alaq
The opening verses of Al-Fatihah
The final verses of Al-Baqarah
The whole of An-Nas

questions.explanation: The narration of the first revelation includes the opening command to read or recite from Al-'Alaq 96:1-5.

questions.question: What does Allah promise concerning the Reminder in Quran 15:9?

options.text: Its preservation depends only on one human family.
He will preserve it.
It will be replaced whenever a ruler chooses.
Only its chapter titles will remain.

questions.explanation: Al-Hijr 15:9 attributes the sending down and preservation of the Reminder to Allah.

questions.question: In Quran 25:1, which term describes the revelation as distinguishing right from wrong?

options.text: Al-Mizan: the Balance
Al-Bayt: the House
Al-Furqan: the Criterion
Al-Jabal: the Mountain

questions.explanation: Al-Furqan 25:1 uses the term Furqan, commonly translated as the Criterion. The question asks about the term in this verse.

questions.question: How does Quran 2:2 describe the Book for those mindful of Allah?

options.text: As a collection of tribal rankings
As a record of business profits
As a list of future calendar dates
As guidance

questions.explanation: Al-Baqarah 2:2 describes the Book as guidance for those who are mindful of Allah.

questions.question: What does Quran 16:98 instruct a person to seek when reciting the Quran?

options.text: Allah's protection from the rejected Satan
Public approval of their voice
A guarantee of worldly wealth
Permission from every listener

questions.explanation: An-Nahl 16:98 instructs the reciter to seek refuge in Allah from Satan.

questions.question: What manner of Quran recitation is instructed in Quran 73:4?

options.text: Rushing so that words merge indistinctly
Measured, deliberate recitation
Reciting only to impress an audience
Changing words to match a preferred rhythm

questions.explanation: Al-Muzzammil 73:4 instructs measured recitation. Speed or performance should not replace attention to the words.

questions.question: According to Quran 38:29, what should people do with the Book's verses?

options.text: Treat reflection as unnecessary.
Read only the chapter titles.
Reflect on them and take heed.
Use the verses only as decoration.

questions.explanation: Sad 38:29 connects the revelation of the blessed Book with reflection on its verses and taking heed.

questions.question: Which reference identifies Ayat al-Kursi?

options.text: Al-Fatihah 1:7
Al-Ikhlas 112:1
An-Nas 114:6
Al-Baqarah 2:255

questions.explanation: Ayat al-Kursi is Al-Baqarah 2:255. The title refers to this particular ayah.

questions.question: Which teaching appears in Quran 2:256?

options.text: There is no compulsion in religion.
Religious belief can be created by physical force.
Family status removes the need for personal belief.
Only wealthy people may learn religion.

questions.explanation: Al-Baqarah 2:256 states that there is no compulsion in religion and distinguishes right guidance from error.

questions.question: Which Quran surah is named after Mary, the mother of Isa (Jesus)?

options.text: Luqman
Maryam
Yusuf
Al-Kahf

questions.explanation: Maryam is the Arabic form of Mary and the name of surah 19.

questions.question: In Quran 12:4, which prophet tells his father about seeing eleven stars, the sun and the moon in a dream?

options.text: Musa (Moses)
Yunus (Jonah)
Yusuf (Joseph)
Sulayman (Solomon)

questions.explanation: Yusuf 12:4 records Yusuf describing this dream to his father.

questions.question: In Quran 20:43, Musa and Harun are instructed to go to whom?

options.text: Luqman
Dhul-Qarnayn
The king in Yusuf's story
Pharaoh

questions.explanation: Taha 20:43 directs Musa and Harun to Pharaoh because he had transgressed.

questions.question: Which surah contains the account of the Companions of the Cave?

options.text: Al-Kahf
Al-Fil
Al-Masad
Al-Kawthar

questions.explanation: Al-Kahf introduces the Companions of the Cave in 18:9 and continues their account in the following verses.

questions.question: In Quran 31:13, to whom does Luqman give advice against associating partners with Allah?

options.text: Pharaoh
His son
A visiting king
A group of merchants

questions.explanation: Luqman 31:13 presents Luqman advising his son. The wording clearly identifies their relationship.

questions.question: In which surah is the account of Dhul-Qarnayn introduced?

options.text: Maryam
Al-Mulk
Al-Kahf
Al-Falaq

questions.explanation: Al-Kahf 18:83 introduces a question about Dhul-Qarnayn and begins the account that follows.

questions.question: In Quran 19:16-22, who receives the announcement of a son and then conceives him?

options.text: The wife of Pharaoh
The queen of Sheba
The sister of Musa
Maryam (Mary)

questions.explanation: These verses narrate the announcement to Maryam and her conception of the child. They form part of the Quran's account of Isa's birth.

questions.question: Which prophet is instructed to build an ark in Quran 11:37?

options.text: Nuh (Noah)
Dawud (David)
Ilyas (Elijah)
Ishaq (Isaac)

questions.explanation: Hud 11:37 records the instruction to Nuh to build the ark under Allah's observation and instruction.

questions.question: Which messenger is named in Quran 37:139-142 in the account involving a great fish?

options.text: Yahya (John)
Yunus (Jonah)
Shu'ayb
Idris

questions.explanation: As-Saffat 37:139 names Yunus; the following verses describe his departure, the ship and the fish.

questions.question: Who raises the foundations of the House alongside Ibrahim in Quran 2:127?

options.text: Ishaq (Isaac)
Ya'qub (Jacob)
Isma'il (Ishmael)
Yusuf (Joseph)

questions.explanation: Al-Baqarah 2:127 names Ibrahim and Isma'il together as they raise the foundations of the House.

questions.question: In Quran 2:34, the angels are instructed to prostrate before whom?

options.text: Nuh (Noah)
Ibrahim (Abraham)
Musa (Moses)
Adam

questions.explanation: Al-Baqarah 2:34 names Adam in this command. The verse also describes Iblis's refusal and arrogance.

questions.question: According to Quran 97:3, Laylat al-Qadr is better than what period?

options.text: A thousand months
A thousand days
A hundred months
A hundred nights

questions.explanation: Al-Qadr 97:3 compares the night favourably with a thousand months. The unit in the verse is months, not days.

questions.question: What does Quran 2:264 warn believers not to do to their charity?

options.text: Give it quietly without seeking recognition.
Invalidate it through reminders of generosity and hurtful treatment.
Give to someone who cannot repay them.
Spend from their lawful earnings.

questions.explanation: Al-Baqarah 2:264 warns against spoiling charity by reminding recipients of favours and causing hurt.

questions.question: Someone assumes the Quran was recited to the people as one complete public address. What does Quran 17:106 clarify?

options.text: It was first revealed only as chapter titles.
Its verses were composed by the audience after each gathering.
It was revealed in stages for deliberate recitation to the people.
Its message did not involve recitation to people.

questions.explanation: Al-Isra 17:106 describes successive revelation and deliberate recitation. This corrects the assumption of a single complete public delivery.

questions.question: Which purpose for revelation in stages is mentioned in Quran 25:32?

options.text: Allowing listeners to choose which verses became revelation
Waiting for political leaders to approve the wording
Replacing the need to remember the revelation
Strengthening the Prophet's heart

questions.explanation: Al-Furqan 25:32 answers an objection about gradual revelation by explaining its role in strengthening the Prophet's heart.

questions.question: A reader cites only the words 'do not approach prayer' from Quran 4:43. What essential condition from the verse have they omitted?

options.text: While intoxicated, until one knows what one is saying
Whenever one has a responsibility to fulfil
Whenever other people can see one praying
After learning the meaning of the prayer

questions.explanation: The opening of An-Nisa 4:43 prohibits approaching prayer while intoxicated until one knows what one is saying. Removing that condition changes the meaning.

questions.question: A reader says the Quran's Arabic form makes understanding its message irrelevant. What feature of Quran 12:2 challenges that claim?

options.text: The verse says its language prevents understanding.
The verse explicitly connects the Arabic revelation with understanding.
The verse limits understanding to knowing chapter numbers.
The verse tells listeners to avoid asking what the message means.

questions.explanation: Yusuf 12:2 identifies the Quran as Arabic so that its audience may understand. The language is not presented as a reason to disregard meaning.

questions.question: In Quran 16:43, how are people who do not know about the earlier messengers directed to resolve their lack of knowledge?

options.text: Decide the matter by the size of a crowd.
Treat every private dream as historical evidence.
Ask those who know the earlier revelation.
Assume that not knowing proves the messengers did not exist.

questions.explanation: An-Nahl 16:43 concerns earlier messengers being men who received revelation and directs those who do not know to ask people of the Reminder.

questions.question: Which response best follows Quran 17:23-24 when an elderly parent becomes difficult to care for?

options.text: Use contemptuous language if care becomes inconvenient.
Assume financial help permits humiliating speech.
Treat old age as a reason to withdraw all kindness.
Speak respectfully and respond with humility and mercy.

questions.explanation: Al-Isra 17:23-24 joins kind treatment of parents with respectful speech, humility, mercy and supplication for them.

questions.question: A person dislikes a group and wants to treat its members unfairly. Which instruction in Quran 5:8 addresses this?

options.text: Do not let hatred lead you away from justice.
Justice is required only toward people you like.
Dislike makes every accusation against a group reliable.
Personal anger replaces the need for fairness.

questions.explanation: Al-Ma'idah 5:8 commands justice and warns that hostility must not lead to injustice.

questions.question: A group makes fun of another group, assuming they are superior. Which reason for restraint appears in Quran 49:11?

options.text: Mockery becomes acceptable when many people join in.
The people mocked may be better than those mocking them.
A popular nickname is automatically respectful.
Wealth gives a group permission to ridicule others.

questions.explanation: Al-Hujurat 49:11 prohibits ridicule and notes that those mocked may be better than those doing the mocking.

questions.question: Which combination of conduct is specifically warned against in Quran 49:12?

options.text: Careful verification, privacy and reconciliation
Respectful disagreement, consultation and patience
Unfounded suspicion, spying and backbiting
Charity, modest speech and gratitude

questions.explanation: Al-Hujurat 49:12 warns against much suspicion, spying and backbiting. The verse does not make every suspicion a proven fact.

questions.question: Which approach to spending matches Quran 25:67?

options.text: Spend everything to gain attention regardless of need.
Refuse every expense even when responsible care is required.
Treat any level of spending as equally balanced.
Avoid extravagance and miserliness, keeping a balanced course.

questions.explanation: Al-Furqan 25:67 describes a middle course between extravagance and stinginess.

questions.question: What practical safeguard does Quran 2:282 prescribe for a debt with a specified term?

options.text: Record it in writing.
Leave the terms deliberately unclear.
Let only the wealthier party decide the amount later.
Assume friendship removes the need for clear terms.

questions.explanation: Al-Baqarah 2:282 gives detailed guidance on recording a debt for a fixed period. Clarity helps protect the parties' rights.

questions.question: According to Quran 49:9-10, what should be sought when groups of believers fight?

options.text: Permanent hostility without attempting settlement
Reconciliation with justice
Automatic support for whichever group is larger
Ignoring injustice to avoid any responsibility

questions.explanation: Al-Hujurat 49:9-10 calls for reconciliation and justice. The call to peace does not remove the requirement of fairness.

questions.question: A person reads Quran 94:5-6 as a promise that every problem must disappear immediately. Which reading is more careful?

options.text: The verses provide a calendar date for every person's relief.
The verses say no believer can ever experience difficulty.
The verses affirm ease with hardship without specifying an immediate timetable for each problem.
The verses make patience and practical effort unnecessary.

questions.explanation: Ash-Sharh 94:5-6 offers reassurance about ease with hardship. It does not give a fixed schedule for each individual's circumstances.

questions.question: What purpose of Quranic accounts is highlighted in Quran 12:111?

options.text: Entertaining people without any guidance
Giving readers permission to invent missing events
Replacing reflection with memorizing character names alone
Providing lessons for people of understanding

questions.explanation: Yusuf 12:111 identifies lessons in the accounts and describes guidance and mercy for believers.

questions.question: Someone gives money generously but also wastes resources carelessly. Which distinction in Quran 17:26-27 matters?

options.text: Giving people their due is encouraged, while wastefulness is condemned.
Any spending labelled generous is automatically free from waste.
Helping relatives is forbidden whenever it involves money.
Wastefulness is defined only by whether an audience approves.

questions.explanation: Al-Isra 17:26-27 combines giving relatives, the needy and travellers their due with a prohibition of wastefulness.

questions.question: According to Quran 3:7, how are the clear verses related to the Book as a whole?

options.text: They may be ignored whenever an ambiguous passage is more exciting.
They form its foundation.
They apply only to the people who first heard them.
They remove the need to believe in the rest of revelation.

questions.explanation: Ali 'Imran 3:7 identifies clear verses as the foundation of the Book and warns about pursuing ambiguity with a distorted purpose.

questions.question: Quran 4:82 invites reflection and mentions the absence of much inconsistency. Which use of the verse best follows its reasoning?

options.text: Assume that thoughtful examination is prohibited.
Resolve every difficulty by ignoring all surrounding verses.
Read and examine the Quran thoughtfully rather than treating apparent difficulty as a reason to stop inquiry.
Treat any reader's first impression as the final meaning.

questions.explanation: An-Nisa 4:82 calls for reflection and connects the Quran's coherence with its divine origin. It encourages thoughtful consideration rather than superficial dismissal.

questions.question: Read together, what do Quran 2:256 and 10:99 teach about trying to force people into belief?

options.text: They say physical force can establish sincere belief in every heart.
They make another person's acceptance entirely controllable by a preacher.
They require rejection of any peaceful explanation of religion.
They reject compulsion and challenge the attempt to compel everyone to believe.

questions.explanation: Al-Baqarah 2:256 states that there is no compulsion in religion. Yunus 10:99 questions compelling people to become believers.

questions.question: Someone quotes only Quran 107:4 to claim that the Quran condemns everyone who prays. What is the main textual problem?

options.text: The following verses identify heedlessness, showing off and withholding small assistance in the description.
The verse does not mention prayer at all.
The following verses state that every form of prayer is forbidden.
The chapter contains no further explanation after verse 4.

questions.explanation: Al-Ma'un 107:4-7 must be read together. Isolating the opening warning removes the description supplied by the subsequent verses.

questions.question: A reader selects an ambiguous passage only to support a pre-existing desire and refuses to consider clear passages. What warning in Quran 3:7 is relevant?

options.text: Any interpretation becomes sound if the reader feels strongly about it.
Pursuing ambiguity to cause discord or force a desired interpretation is criticized.
Ambiguous passages are the only verses with religious value.
Clear passages may be set aside whenever they challenge a preference.

questions.explanation: Ali 'Imran 3:7 warns against the misuse of ambiguous passages. The question does not require choosing between scholarly positions on where to pause in the verse.

questions.question: Quran 97:1 mentions revelation on Laylat al-Qadr, while 17:106 describes revelation in stages. Which is the most careful initial conclusion?

options.text: The mention of a night proves that the Prophet delivered the entire Quran in one public sitting.
The mention of stages proves that Laylat al-Qadr has no connection to revelation.
Both descriptions must be considered; neither verse should simply be discarded to preserve an assumption.
Readers must choose one verse as true and the other as false.

questions.explanation: The verses describe the Quran's descent and its successive revelation. They should be studied together rather than forced into an unsupported either-or claim.

questions.question: Quran 2:106 discusses abrogation or replacement of a revelation. Does that alone allow a reader to declare any disliked instruction abrogated?

options.text: Yes; disliking an instruction is sufficient evidence that it has been abrogated.
Yes; a popular online opinion automatically establishes abrogation.
No; the verse denies that Allah can replace any revelation.
No; the verse does not authorize personal preference to establish a specific claim of abrogation.

questions.explanation: Al-Baqarah 2:106 discusses Allah's authority over revelation. A specific claim that one ruling supersedes another requires evidence, not personal preference.

questions.question: Why is it mistaken to infer that Al-Fatihah was the first passage revealed simply because it appears first in the mushaf?

options.text: Written order and revelation chronology are different, and the first-revelation narration points to Al-'Alaq.
The first page of every book must record its earliest historical event.
Al-Fatihah is not part of the Quran.
The first-revelation narration identifies An-Nas instead.

questions.explanation: The surah index begins with Al-Fatihah, while Sahih al-Bukhari 3 describes the opening revelation from Al-'Alaq. These concern different kinds of order.

questions.question: Someone says the Quran gives the Messenger no role in explaining revelation. Which passage most directly challenges this?

options.text: Quran 12:4, which recounts Yusuf's dream.
Quran 16:44, which assigns him the task of explaining what was sent down to people.
Quran 18:83, which introduces Dhul-Qarnayn.
Quran 97:3, which describes Laylat al-Qadr's value.

questions.explanation: An-Nahl 16:44 explicitly connects the sending down of the Reminder with the Messenger explaining it to people so they may reflect.

questions.question: A storyteller adds invented dialogue to a Quranic account and presents the dialogue as Allah's revealed words. What distinction is essential?

options.text: An uplifting lesson automatically turns invented wording into revelation.
Details become Quranic whenever the audience enjoys them.
A teaching illustration must be distinguished from what the Quran actually states.
Any dialogue associated with a prophet must appear in the Quran.

questions.explanation: Yusuf 12:111 describes the revealed account as truth and guidance. A narrator's additions are not made Quranic by having a useful lesson.

questions.question: Someone uses Quran 2:286 to claim that a believer will never experience exhaustion or need help. Which response is most careful?

options.text: The verse states that asking anyone for help is forbidden.
The verse promises unlimited physical strength to every believer.
The verse requires ignoring illness when evaluating one's capacity.
The verse concerns responsibility within capacity; it does not promise that people never become tired or need support.

questions.explanation: Al-Baqarah 2:286 states that Allah does not burden a soul beyond its capacity. This should not be turned into a claim that fatigue or a need for help is impossible.

questions.question: A reader studies Quran 33:32 and ignores its opening address to the Prophet's wives. What should be checked before generalizing every detail?

options.text: Who is addressed and how the surrounding passage frames the instruction.
Only whether the verse contains a memorable phrase.
Whether the reader prefers the instruction to apply universally.
Only the verse's position on a printed page.

questions.explanation: Al-Ahzab 33:32 explicitly addresses the Prophet's wives. Identifying the addressees and context is necessary before making interpretive claims about wider application.

questions.question: In Quran 5:89, what distinction prevents the conclusion that every casual expression has identical consequences?

options.text: The distinction between oaths spoken indoors and outdoors
The distinction between unintentional oaths and deliberately binding oaths
The distinction between a wealthy speaker and a poor speaker
The distinction between short and long sentences

questions.explanation: Al-Ma'idah 5:89 distinguishes unintentional oaths from deliberate ones and then discusses expiation. Specific personal cases require more detail than this quiz provides.

questions.question: After reading Quran 20:114, a learner concludes that gaining some knowledge removes any need to keep learning. Which feature of the verse challenges that?

options.text: The verse says knowledge has no role in understanding revelation.
The verse makes every learner equally knowledgeable.
The Prophet is instructed to ask his Lord for an increase in knowledge.
The verse says uncertainty should always be hidden.

questions.explanation: Taha 20:114 includes a supplication for increased knowledge. It supports humility and continuing to learn rather than claiming completeness.

questions.question: Someone claims a Quran verse gives them the exact calendar date of the Hour. Which principle in Quran 7:187 most directly tests that claim?

options.text: The most popular prediction determines its timing.
Anyone who knows Arabic automatically knows its date.
The date is assigned by each generation's scholars.
Knowledge of its timing belongs to Allah.

questions.explanation: Al-A'raf 7:187 places knowledge of the Hour's timing with Allah and describes its sudden arrival. A claimed date requires scrutiny rather than automatic acceptance.
